# parity-fuzz --mode zcalc baseline: normalized signatures of KNOWN gaps.
# A divergence whose signature is here is allowed; a NEW one fails CI.
# Regenerate: parity-fuzz --mode zcalc --count N --verify 3  (copy NEW-signature lines).
#
# No known gaps. zcalc is an autoload FUNCTION (Functions/Misc/zcalc) that zshrs
# intercepts with a native Rust impl (ext_builtins.rs zcalc), so this mode pins
# the impl against the real function. Fixed on introduction, not baselined:
#
#   1. zcalc:133 `zmodload -i zsh/mathfunc` — zcalc pulls in the math library on
#      startup, which is the whole reason `zcalc -e 'sqrt(16)'` resolves while a
#      bare `$(( sqrt(16) ))` does not (the named-function table is empty until
#      the module boots, math.rs:2519). The native impl never loaded it, so
#      EVERY math function zcalc exists to provide answered "unknown function".
#   2. zcalc:99-112 `zcalc_show_value` — the result is REFORMATTED, not echoed:
#        - contains `.` → printf `%2$g` (6 significant digits), so `atan(1)*4`
#          is 3.14159, not the expansion's 3.1415926535897931;
#        - ends in a bare `.` → printed raw, so `sqrt(16)` keeps zsh's `4.`;
#        - no `.` → `printf "%d"`, a CONVERSION: `1/0` under -f is Inf, which
#          renders as ZLONG_MAX (9223372036854775807), and NaN renders as 0.
#      Formatting must go through the PRINTF conversion
#      (builtin.rs format_spec_float_conv), NOT `convfloat`: the float-parameter
#      formatter re-appends a trailing `.` when %g yields none
#      (params.rs:10770, c:params.c:5748-5749), which printed `sqrt(2)*sqrt(2)`
#      as `2.` where zsh prints `2`.
#   3. A failed evaluation prints its diagnostic and NO value — the expansion
#      never produced one. arithsubst reports the error and returns "0", which
#      was printed as a result, so `zcalc -e '1/0'` answered `0`.
#
# STDERR-only difference, invisible to this mode's default gate (stdout + exit)
# and surfaced only under --stderr: zsh's zcalc evaluates through `eval`, so an
# arithmetic error is tagged `(eval):1: division by zero` where the native impl
# says `zsh:1:`. Same context-tag class as the zmv baseline's `zmv:239:` —
# reproducing it means faking an eval frame around a native builtin.
#
# Any divergence here is a regression.
